title: Hope in Resurrection
english: He was about at once to be burned up with the cities and himself the ill-famed temple; houses too to be smoked, shaken by earthquakes.

That moreover before the day of the great and manifest one, in which to all the divine judgment-seat of Christ giving to each according to his works will be set forth, these things will happen to the Jews, he foretold saying: Before the coming of the day of the Lord the great and manifest.
Moreover also my flesh will encamp upon hope.
Of Cyril. For he rose again three-day, because it was not possible for life existing according to nature him to be held fast by the bonds of death.
And again: Not indeed it is lawful to say corruption to be able ever to hold fast the flesh united to the Word, and to be a dwelling place of them the gates of Hades the divine to become soul.
For he was not left in Hades, as also the blessed Peter said: That you will not leave my soul in Hades, nor will you give your holy one to see corruption.
Of Cyril. For he rose again having spoiled Hades, and to those in bonds saying: Come forth; and to those in darkness: Be revealed.
He made known to me ways of life.
and as upon us the first calling beautiful.
translator_notes: The Greek is fragmented at the end of p20 with 'upon us the', suggesting a cut mid-phrase; no completion attempted.
p6, p12, p18 are editorial attributions ('Κυρίλλου', 'Κυρίλλου Ἀλεξανδρείας') and treated as non-content; skipped per instructions.
p5 contains '74.761' which appears as a stray digit or folio marker; omitted as non-content.
The text switches between oratio obliqua and direct speech; preserved as given.
Some phrases like 'shmeared' or unclear compounds are rendered literally per lexicon; no conjectural emendation.

title: Divine Humility and Authority
english: The participation in heavenly goods is a gift that has been added to human nature, and somehow, human poverty has enriched us.
God raised Jesus Christ from the dead, and he has been presented before you in a state of health.

It is clear that the Father's act of raising Jesus Christ from the dead refers to his flesh, and no one would doubt this, since Jesus himself, as the life-giving and active power of the Father, gives life to his own body, as he said, 'Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it' (John 2:19).
The body that Jesus vivifies is not foreign to him, but his own, which is the body of the Word.

I urge you, men, brothers, and fathers, to listen to me and prepare yourselves for the benevolent, by bending your ear to understand the subtle power of divine words, as it is written, 'Go out from your land and from your kin' (Genesis 12:1).
It is evident that those who follow God completely and in every way, making hope in him second to their fleshly and worldly desires, will richly receive the blessing from above.
Moses was educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he was powerful in his words and deeds, and when he was forty years old, he was prepared to fulfill God's plan.
Jesus said, 'I was not sent except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel' (Matthew 15:24), because the promises were made to them, and their fathers were the recipients of these promises.
We do not deny that the Word from God the Father, who became a man, has come among us, and we acknowledge that, being rich, he became poor and emptied himself.
However, the one who does injustice to his neighbor pushed Jesus away, saying, 'Who appointed you as ruler and judge over us? Do you want to destroy me as you destroyed the Egyptian yesterday?'
The Israelites could not endure the divine glory of the Son, who was showing himself and bringing knowledge, and this would be a sign for us that they could not bear his glory.
As Jesus said, he did not come to destroy, but the one who does injustice to his neighbor said, 'Who appointed you as ruler and judge over us?'
Jesus said, 'I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob' (Exodus 3:6).

The divine Moses was called as the one who took away the Egyptian, although the Egyptian was oppressing and being insolent, but Jesus, casting out evil demons as into an abyss, and not willingly changing the tyranny over us, was said to cast them out through the power of Beelzebub, the ruler of demons.

The God of all things reveals himself, but when he reveals himself, Moses turns away his face, and this would be a sign for us that the Israelites could not endure the divine glory of the Son, who was showing himself and bringing knowledge.

Moses was educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he was powerful in his words and deeds, and when he was forty years old, he was prepared to fulfill God's plan, and thus, the blessing from above will richly abound for those who follow God completely and in every way, and who have made hope in him second to their fleshly and worldly desires.
translator_notes: The Greek text may be fragmented, and some sentences may be cut off at the edges.
The translation of 'ἐπεί πως' as 'somehow' is an attempt to convey the reason for human enrichment.
The phrase 'τῇ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου φύσει' is translated as 'human nature', indicating the recipient of the action.
The word 'ἐν τούτῳ οὖτος' is translated as 'he', referring back to the subject of the sentence, Jesus Christ.
The allusion to 2 Corinthians 8:9 is based on the phrase 'being rich, he became poor', which is a reference to Christ's humility.

title: Removal of Corruption
english: The sandal of your feet is a sign of death and corruption, for every sandal is a remnant of a dead and corrupted animal, and thus Christ is inaccessible to those who are still bound by the law and pedagogical worship.

It is necessary to remove the stain and the dirt from sin, and to wipe away the dirt that comes from sin, which includes removing the filth that arises from sin, and also to remove the defilement and to scrape off the dirt that comes from sin, in order to be transplanted beyond Babylon.
You have filled up the evil of the Moabites, neighbor of Damascus, therefore you will be expelled from Damascus to Babylon.
Jacob asked to find a dwelling place for God, saying that he would not rest until he found the place of the Lord and the dwelling of God, which is clearly Christ (Genesis 28:22).
However, Solomon built a house for him, but the Most High does not dwell in handmade temples (1 Kings 8:27).

The wise Solomon built a famous temple in Jerusalem, and the crowd of Jews was very pleased with it, thinking that God had dwelled in it, but they were slow to understand and ignorant of the words of God.

They thought Jerusalem was the city of God and that he dwelled only in it, but God rebukes those who think small, saying, 'What kind of house will you build for me, who has the heaven as a throne and the earth as a footstool?' (Isaiah 66:1-2, Acts 7:49-50).
Stephen was stoned, calling out and saying, 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit' (Acts 7:59).
As the holy Cyril says, I commit my spirit into your hands.
This is a great and extraordinary achievement for our souls, as Stephen, with his knees down, cried out with a loud voice, saying, 'Lord, do not hold this sin against them' (Luke 23:34, Acts 7:60).
After saying this, he fell asleep.
Saul was in agreement with his murder.

Stephen's prayer was not just a simple one, but one that was said with attention and care, as he was apologizing, saying that not even the previous things were of anger, he says, 'Lord', and wanting to draw them to this.
For just as he was apologizing, he was able to leave his anger and wrath behind, and cleanse his soul of the passion, making his words acceptable.

In the introductions of his preaching, Stephen was like a river flowing above the rest, silencing all his opponents and stopping the shameless tongues of the Jews, who were unable to withstand him, as he was confounding all the Jewish things, and setting up a bright trophy and a manifest victory.
He was a generous and wise man, full of grace, and his preaching benefited the Church greatly, even though he did not preach for a long time.
Unfortunately, he was suddenly seized and condemned as a blasphemer, and stoned.
